skill.name: create-plan
skill.description: Creates concise, repository-aware implementation plans for coding tasks when users explicitly request planning.
skill.summary: Turn coding requests into scoped, ordered plans with validation and risk checks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only, read-only, and contains no command execution or semantic security concerns.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown backticks to format documentation paths such as README.md and docs/. It contains no Ruby syntax, shell command, or execution instruction.
Lines 42-63 are a fenced Markdown example showing the required plan format. The backticks delimit documentation content and do not execute a command.

content.value_statement: Coding requests can lack scope, sequence, and validation details. This skill reviews repository context and produces a concise implementation plan with ordered actions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews repository documentation and relevant files in read-only mode.
Identifies languages, frameworks, test commands, and deployment constraints.
Defines concise in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries.
Produces six to ten ordered, verb-first implementation steps.
Includes validation, edge-case, risk, and rollout actions when relevant.
Lists up to three unresolved questions without blocking reasonable assumptions.
limitations: Does not edit files or implement the proposed changes.
Does not guarantee that every relevant file is identified during a quick review.
Requires accessible repository context for file-specific recommendations.
May ask one or two questions when essential requirements are missing.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature
use_cases.description: Convert a feature request into scoped changes, tests, risks, and rollout actions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactor
use_cases.description: Map a refactoring goal to affected modules, safe sequencing, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Review Delivery Scope
use_cases.description: Create an implementation outline that clarifies boundaries and open decisions before work begins.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Coding Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan to add [feature] to this repository. Include scope, ordered actions, tests, and relevant risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a clear feature request with repository access.

prompt_templates.title: Bug Fix Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan how to diagnose and fix [problem]. Identify likely files, reproduction steps, regression tests, edge cases, and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a defect needs investigation before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Refactoring Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only plan for refactoring [component]. Preserve [behavior], identify dependencies, sequence migrations, and include rollback checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for structural changes that must preserve existing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-System Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [change] across [systems]. Cover contracts, data migration, compatibility, observability, staged rollout, rollback, tests, and unresolved decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced work spanning services or deployment boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a plan to add passwordless sign-in to the web application.
output: Scope: Add email-based sign-in while preserving current sessions. Exclude unrelated account settings.
Action: Trace authentication routes, session storage, email delivery, and existing test coverage.
Action: Define token lifetime, single-use behavior, invalidation, rate limits, and audit events.
Validation: Add tests for expired, reused, malformed, and cross-account tokens.
Open question: Which email provider and delivery environment should the implementation use?

output_examples.input: Plan a database client refactor without changing public behavior.
output: Scope: Replace internal client usage while keeping public interfaces stable.
Action: Inventory construction, query, transaction, and shutdown paths.
Action: Introduce the replacement behind existing interfaces and migrate callers in dependency order.
Validation: Run unit and integration suites, then compare query and error behavior.
Risk: Preserve transaction boundaries, connection cleanup, and deployment rollback.

best_practices: Provide a specific outcome and explain important constraints.
Name behaviors that must remain unchanged.
Share repository context, acceptance criteria, and deployment requirements.
anti_patterns: Request a plan when immediate implementation is required.
Omit essential business rules and expect precise technical scope.
Treat the generated plan as proof that implementation will succeed.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repository files?
faq.answer: No. It reviews available context in read-only mode and returns only a plan.

faq.question: What does the plan include?
faq.answer: It includes intent, scope, ordered actions, validation, relevant risks, and up to three open questions.

faq.question: When will the skill ask questions?
faq.answer: It asks one or two questions only when missing information prevents responsible planning.

faq.question: Can it plan changes across several services?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide system boundaries, contracts, deployment constraints, and required compatibility behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate implementation code?
faq.answer: No. The output remains implementation-agnostic and does not include code snippets.

faq.question: How detailed are the action items?
faq.answer: The default plan contains six to ten atomic steps with relevant files, commands, tests, and rollout details.
